summary.headline: Greenlam Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue up 8% YoY to INR875 crores, EBITDA down 19% to INR87 crores as laminate sales volume fell 12%.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 net revenue rose 8% YoY to INR875 crores, but gross margin fell 310 bps to 51.5% and EBITDA before forex fell 19% to INR87 crores (9.9% margin). Laminates, the core business, showed no growth in the quarter, with export volumes hit by container, vessel and freight issues and domestic affected by a high base from last year's flagship catalogue launch. Plywood and allied losses narrowed and chipboard turned EBITDA-positive for a second quarter. H1 consolidated revenue grew 13% to INR1,672 crores, with H1 EBITDA up 4% to INR168 crores; net debt fell INR19 crores since March to INR922 crores. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to 16-18% and expects H2 to be better than H1, but gave no H2 margin guidance.

segments.name: Laminates & allied
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue flat YoY at INR658 crores; EBITDA margin before forex 12%, down 590 bps YoY. Sales volume 5.09 million sheets, down 12% YoY, mainly exports; production 4.83 million sheets at 79% utilisation. Realisation INR1,241 per sheet, up 12% YoY. H1 revenue +3% to INR1,254 crores, H1 margin 12.9% (down 290 bps per errata).

segments.name: Plywood & allied (plywood, decorative veneer, engineered floors, engineered doors)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue +7.5% YoY to INR110 crores; EBITDA loss before forex narrowed to INR1.4 crores. Plywood sales volume 1.94 million sq m (+23% YoY) at INR257 per sq m (+4%); plywood utilisation 46%. H1 revenue +13.5% to INR216 crores, H1 EBITDA loss INR6.6 crores. Veneer, engineered floors and engineered doors reported as EBITDA positive.

segments.name: Panel & allied (chipboard)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR107 crores (more than doubled YoY, per errata +124%); EBITDA before forex INR9 crores (about 8%). Sales volume 46,871 cubic metres (+78% YoY); realisation INR22,591 per cubic metre (+24%); utilisation 61%. H1 revenue INR202 crores (+156%), H1 EBITDA INR12 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 16-18%, versus earlier 18-20% guidance; H2 expected to be better than H1 as export challenges ease.
No specific H2 margin guidance; management says H2 margin intended to be better than H1.
Laminates FY27 growth now expected at roughly 10-12% or slightly below, versus earlier 10-12% guidance; management says Q2 is an aberration.
Net debt reduction for FY27 expected near the earlier INR100 crore target, contingent on revenue and margin recovery; H1 reduction was INR19 crores.
Plywood expected to reach full capacity utilisation around FY29; plywood EBITDA expected to turn positive going forward.
Andhra Pradesh two new laminate lines expected to begin commercial production by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Two new laminate lines under way at Andhra Pradesh plant, on schedule for commercial production by Q4 FY27; after these, AP has five laminate lines with capacity for three more, and could reach eight laminate lines plus two board lines.
Current asset base, including the two AP lines at full capacity, could deliver about INR4,800-5,000 crores revenue depending on pricing.
Laminate production 4.83 million sheets in Q2 (79% utilisation); H1 9.73 million sheets (79%).

Plywood capacity utilisation 46% in Q2 and 42% in H1; one plywood plant seen as capable of about INR450 crores revenue at current pricing and mix, and at least one more plywood plant needed to reach about INR1,000 crores.
Chipboard plant (about 300,000 cubic metre line in AP) running at 61% utilisation for 18 months; management says highest-cost environment currently.
Management says little capex needed for engineered floors and doors, with capital employed not increased in last couple of years.
demand_pricing: Laminate export sales hit by container and vessel availability, freight cost, longer transit times and competitive landscape; management says the issue was logistics rather than demand.
Domestic laminates hit by high base from last year's flagship catalogue launch.
Europe market not growing and local manufacturers struggling; management says company is winning share, sees no material demand destruction for itself.
Plywood expanding in South, West (added about a year ago) and East India; tier-two brand launched in October 2026 for southern markets only to address volume.
Chipboard: HMR about 15-20% of segment revenue; pre-laminated products about 45-50% of volume; competition in chipboard noted.
Trade volumes in October-November: signs better than last year, but Diwali timing shifts make comparison not like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: Was the laminate degrowth due to a high base and was it domestic or international led? A peer export-focused saw no degrowth.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was partly high base domestically (flagship catalogue launched last year) and export shortfall due to container and vessel shortages, high freight and longer transit; a mix of both.

qa_highlights.question: Will the lost international revenue be recorded later or is it lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh Mittal said it cannot be said to be lost and that international numbers will improve in subsequent periods.

qa_highlights.question: Plywood ramp-up: when can utilisation be optimal and what levers are there?
qa_highlights.answer: Full plywood capacity utilisation seen possible around FY29; levers are secondary sales expansion, network build-out and the new tier-two brand launched in October for South India.

qa_highlights.question: Can the current asset base support INR6,000-7,000 crores revenue at optimum utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No; current base with two AP lines could deliver about INR5,000 crores revenue, depending on pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Returns outlook for plywood, chipboard and new businesses versus laminates (about 14% margin, 20% ROCE per earlier commentary)?
qa_highlights.answer: Laminates earn about 30% pre-tax ROCE on existing capital in H1; plywood is subscale with one plant; chipboard in highest-cost phase; further volume needed to lift asset turns.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of European demand and freight conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees market challenge with no organic growth in Europe but expects to keep winning share; no major demand destruction seen for the company.

qa_highlights.question: Product mix and HMR contribution in chipboard?
qa_highlights.answer: HMR about 15-20% of segment revenue; pre-laminated products 45-50% of volume, improving each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue guidance, H2 profitability and debt reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth guided at 16-18%; no H2 margin guidance but expected better than H1; debt reduction likely near INR100 crores for the year though H1 was lower.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 10-12% laminate growth guidance still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects laminate growth to be in that range but possibly below 10-12%.

risks_watch: Laminate export recovery depends on container, vessel and freight normalisation; first sign of a recovery in Q3 is critical.
Laminate growth guidance now at risk of falling below 10-12%; first-ever flat laminate quarter in several years.
Chipboard running at 61% utilisation in a high-cost environment with rising competition.
Plywood remains subscale and loss-making at EBITDA level; needs more distribution and possibly another plant.
Net debt reduction behind the INR100 crore plan; H1 reduction only INR19 crores.
European demand weakness and raw material price swings affecting gross margin (down 310 bps YoY in Q2).
summary.management_tone: Candid and somewhat defensive: management said it was not satisfied with Q2, attributed the miss mainly to logistics and export issues, and called the quarter an aberration. Confidence is expressed for H2 recovery, but margin guidance was withheld and laminate and debt targets were softened.
key_quotes: Q2 should be seen as an aberration, and we are quite confident on driving back the business to a better profit margin and a better revenue growth.
I think it's a demand side, it's a sales marketing side which we have to kind of improve so we can drive more utilization, which will lead to better profitability.
On a full capacity utilization, I think probably FY 2029 will be a relevant year where we can have a full capacity utilization.
